lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Performance task planning: comparing real numbers

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example shows how to justify a modelling choice.

items.prompt: Order √10, 3, and 10/3 from least to greatest.

steps: Recheck exactly with a common denominator of 9: 9 < 10 < 100/9 · 9 = 100, so 81 < 90 < 100 confirms 3 < √10 < 10/3.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Decide what the quantities are before you compute anything.

items.prompt: Which whole number is closest to √97 - 2?
A square garden has an area of 200 square inches. Between which two consecutive whole numbers of inches is the side length?
A student claims √257 > 20 because 257 > 20. Which statement correctly analyzes the claim?
choices: The claim cannot be evaluated without a calculator.

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Plan in writing: what you will model, why that model, and how you will check it.

items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
